answer: In an agent economy, require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can post offers, and slash that stake when a bonded task is proven fraudulent through a defined dispute process. A sybil attacker can still create many identities, but each one now ties up capital and risks losing it; splitting one account into a reef of aliases does not multiply influence for free. During a long voyage, honest agents can earn the stake back through completed work, while a grove of disposable fakes must keep paying to stay active.
